scraped.scraped_description: Landlord Tech—in industry so-called property tech or proptech—is leading to new forms of housing injustice in ways that increase the power of landlords and further disempower tenants and those seeking shelter.

name: Landlord Tech Watch
tagline: Producing data, scholarship, and popular educational materials documenting how property technology increases landlord power while disempowering tenants
sdg_alignment: SDG 16 – Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions

academic_citations.title: The work of landlord technology: The fictions of frictionless property management
Hormonal Advantage: Retracing Exploitative Histories of Workplace Menstrual Tracking
The Work of Watching One Another: Lateral Surveillance, Risk, and Governance

documented_limitations: Page requires JavaScript to render; content not accessible via static HTML
curation_criteria: Documentation of landlord technology platforms that impact tenant rights; focus on surveillance, eviction facilitation, and data collection practices
contributor_governance: Open contribution model through GitHub; maintained by Anti-Eviction Mapping Project core team
policy_outcomes: Provides action plan for tenants to defend themselves from landlord tech; maintains deployment map to track landlord technology installations
political_relevance_summary: Landlord Tech Watch addresses empowering advocacy and civic campaigning and making civic data accessible and actionable. It has documented policy impact.

movement_building_utility.notes: Amplifies advocacy efforts through Producing data, scholarship, and popular educational materials documenting how property technology increases landlord power while disempowering tenants.

generalizability_notes: Open-source codebase enables replication. currently deployed in United States only, but approach could be adapted to other national contexts.
